title: The normalized comparison for a Koszul-regular quotient is invertible
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, I an ideal, n,r natural numbers, and f:Fin r -> A a Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence] with span(range f)=I. Then the unique normalized map selfTorConormalComparison A I n [new-r4-self-tor-conormal-comparison] from the nth exterior conormal module to Tor_n^A(A/I,A/I) is an isomorphism of A-modules, including n=0, r=0, and I=A.

source.place: lemma-divided-powers-on-tor; Tags 062I and 06YH for conormal and derived tensor

proof.text: Obtain the Koszul conormal basis b and the normalized Koszul projective resolution P with a:K(f) isomorphic to P.complex and a_0 followed by P.pi_0 equal to the quotient augmentation. The augmented refinement is necessary because the older existence theorem fixes the complex but not the augmentation.

Apply the quotient-coefficient Koszul homology basis calculation to b. It gives an isomorphism e from the exterior conormal module to H_n(K(f) tensor A/I), carrying each increasing exterior basis vector to the corresponding Koszul cycle class.

Use the normalization of selfTorConormalComparison with the ideal lifts of f, a.hom, and the supplied basis cycles. It identifies c followed by the projective-resolution Tor comparison with e followed by the homology map of a. Extend this equality from the exterior basis to every element by its finite basis expansion, lifting each A/I coefficient to A. Since the other three arrows are isomorphisms, cancellation writes c as their composite and its invertibility follows.
